=== METHOD ===
The full one-hour soak Z-056 deferred to this slice, run with the banked Z-056 harness exactly as designed: run_z056.sh start hidden_files/z057_soak 3600 60, detached (setsid + nohup), launched by the previous team-01 lead at 09:08 EST (2026-11-12T14:08:15Z). Both legs ran the full 3600 s concurrently, pinned mimir -c 2 / glibc -c 3, sampling every 60 s plus t=0 and the deadline: 61 scheduled samples per leg (t = 0, 60, ..., 3600). Workload, sampling and integrity checks are as specified in the Z-056 recorded run: 320-slot mixed lifecycle, fixed-seed distribution 55% small (16..1024 B) / 25% medium (4 KiB..64 KiB) / 20% large (128 KiB..2 MiB), dense-touch, per-sample stored-byte verification of every live block (first/middle/last), calloc zero-fill and realloc contents-preservation verified, smaps_rollup Rss/Pss plus maps VMA and allocation-window hole reads per sample, timed latency batches (256 x 64 B + 32 x 64 KiB alloc/free); after the deadline each probe frees everything and emits DRAINED and DONE. Time-boxed, not op-boxed: the legs share duration and workload distribution, not the operation sequence, so per-leg drift curves are comparable as resident-shape series, never as equal-work measurements. Collect: run_z056.sh collect hidden_files/z057_soak verified both exit codes (0 and 0) and ran the summariser; collect exit 0. Raw files: hidden_files/z057_soak/z056_mimir.raw and z056_glibc.raw (team-local), appended verbatim below; both .err files are empty (0 bytes).

=== READING - THE ONE-HOUR SOAK (roadmap gate) ===
Gate: "soak report (drift curves, worst fragmentation, tail RSS)" - MET. Both legs COMPLETE: 61 of 61 scheduled samples each (t = 0, 60, ..., 3600), DRAINED + DONE present, both probes exited 0, summariser verdict ALL LEGS COMPLETE, collect exit 0. The full per-sample drift series for both legs is in the SUMMARY above and the RAW appendix below.

F1 - No drift over the hour (the soak question). mimir Rss median over the first 30 live samples 151,822 KiB vs 148,730 KiB over the last 30 - flat to slightly DOWN, no upward trend; the final live sample (133,816 KiB) sits below the hour median (150,812 KiB), and peak Rss (179,672 KiB) occurs early, at t=720, not at the tail. glibc is likewise flat (190,914 -> 187,950 KiB first-half vs second-half medians). mimir net_factor median 1.988 across the whole hour. Neither allocator degrades or bloats over 256,120,832 (mimir) / 1,628,749,056 (glibc) lifecycle operations.
F2 - Resident shape: the Z-056 pilot result HOLDS at 6x duration. mimir net_factor median 1.988 / worst 2.469 vs glibc 2.500 / 3.168; peak Rss mimir 179,672 KiB vs glibc 204,084 KiB on near-equal live peaks (105,892,768 B vs 98,299,712 B). Grade in roadmap words for the soak workload: WIN on resident shape (this workload, this machine, this shared-host window).
F3 - Worst fragmentation (mimir allocation-VMA window): median 108 holes carrying a median 52,664,320 hole bytes at live samples; worst total hole bytes 76,947,456 B at t=2280; worst hole count 123; worst single largest hole 24,289,280 B; worst net_factor sample 2.469 at t=1320. glibc's window shows 0 holes at every sample - its fragmentation cost appears as the higher net_factor of F2, exactly as in the pilot. Address holes and resident holes remain different quantities.
F4 - Tail RSS and drain retention. mimir final live sample Rss 133,816 KiB; after freeing all 320 blocks in-process, DRAINED Rss 38,772 KiB (retained net 36,696 KiB over the t=0 baseline of 2,076 KiB, vma_delta +73) - the Z-048 mapping-cache and retention posture, essentially unchanged from the pilot's 36,100 KiB net after only 600 s: retention does NOT grow with soak duration. glibc DRAINED Rss 186,480 KiB equals its final live sample (retained net 184,392 KiB, vma_delta 0) - in-process arena/top retention, returned at exit. Process exit returns everything for both legs.
F5 - Throughput and latency (shared-machine samples, NOT baselines). glibc executed 1,628,749,056 ops vs mimir 256,120,832 in the same hour (6.36x, matching the pilot's 6.29x); the legs are therefore not equal-work measurements (see METHOD). Latency batches are flat all hour with no degradation trend: small median 253 ns/op mimir (worst sample 329) vs 44 glibc (worst 70); large median 2,423 ns/op mimir (worst 2,915) vs 134 glibc (worst 191) - LOSS on batch latency, same shape as the pilot.
F6 - Integrity. Neither leg aborted. Every sample of both legs verified the stored bytes of all live blocks (first/middle/last), every calloc fill verified zeroed, every realloc verified contents-preserved - 61 samples x 2 legs with zero mismatches; both probes exited 0 and both .err files are empty. No allocator bug was discovered by the soak, and no bug in this slice's tooling was found (the harness ran exactly as banked at Z-056).
Team structure: the soak was launched by the previous team-01 lead (cancelled mid-slice with the soak detached and healthy). The finishing lead (keeper restart) verified the live soak from disk, waited for both legs to exit, collected with the Z-056 tooling, ran the standing gate on the final tree and assembled this run, running the six Mythic Engineering roles (method, code, statistics, gate, ledger, risk) sequentially itself; no sub-agent spawn was used for the finishing phase, recorded plainly per the campaign rule.
